outcome: Two independent, non-peer-reviewed preprints in 2026 claim full proofs of Crouzeix's conjecture (sharp constant 2): a July 27, 2026 manuscript by neurosurgeon Shanmu Jin, produced with substantial assistance from OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and informally reviewed (but not formally refereed) by Anne Greenbaum, Alex Townsend and Michel Crouzeix himself; and an independent, differently-argued proof posted August 4, 2026 by Emiel Lorist and Felix Schwenninger, who used the same model only to explore proof strategies. Neither had completed conventional peer review as of the most recent secondary reporting (mid-August 2026), so the conjecture is not yet counted as resolved by these rules.

ai.basis_quote: Jin reportedly used 'OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol' in what was described as 'an autonomous run lasting about 16 hours' — 'a long-running research system exploring arguments, checking paths, and developing a candidate result.' Jin himself had to recognize relevance, convert findings into coherent proof form, and assume manuscript responsibility. Separately, the GitHub repository's README states: 'OpenAI ChatGPT contributed to proof development, manuscript preparation, and adversarial checking.'

disputes.summary: Two independent proofs of the same 22-year-old conjecture appeared eight days apart in 2026: Shanmu Jin's GPT-5.6-Sol-assisted proof (preprints.org, July 27, 2026) and Emiel Lorist and Felix Schwenninger's independently-derived, differently-argued proof (arXiv:2608.03841, August 4, 2026, revised August 17, 2026). The two used unrelated arguments (Jin's approach vs. Lorist-Schwenninger's double-layer-potential/2-dilation perturbation lemma), and neither cites the other as dependent. A third party, Qinyu Luo (ByteDance), separately published a 'Defect-Gram' proof and a Lean 4 formalization of a related candidate proof on Zenodo in August 2026, apparently as an independent reproduction/verification effort rather than a claim of separate priority.

summary: As of the most recent reporting (mid-to-late August 2026), Crouzeix's conjecture — that the matrix norm of f(A) is at most twice the sup of |f| on the field of values of A — has two independent, non-peer-reviewed claimed proofs, both from 2026, both post-dating the January 2024 frozen revision. (1) Shanmu Jin, a neurosurgery resident at Peking Union Medical College Hospital with no formal advanced-mathematics background, posted a manuscript on preprints.org on July 27, 2026 (preprints.org/manuscript/202607.1919; mirrored with a Lean 4 formalization and a public, privacy-filtered AI-conversation record at github.com/jinshanmu/CrouzeixConjecture). By his and secondary accounts (SIAM News essay by Alex Townsend, SCMP, remio.ai), the key argument was produced by an approximately 16-hour autonomous run of OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, with Jin recognizing its relevance and converting it into a coherent manuscript; the repo's own README credits 'OpenAI ChatGPT' with 'proof development, manuscript preparation, and adversarial checking.' Numerical analysts Anne Greenbaum and Alex Townsend, and Michel Crouzeix himself, examined the proof informally and believed it correct, but this is expert digestion short of formal peer review or journal acceptance — so per §6.1 the correct code is `claimed`, not `resolved`. (2) Independently, Emiel Lorist and Felix Schwenninger posted a five-to-ten-page proof via a different operator-theoretic route (double-layer potential representation plus a perturbation lemma for 2-dilations) as arXiv:2608.03841 on August 4, 2026 (v2 August 17, 2026, expanded from 7 to 10 pages). Their own AI disclosure states GPT-5.6 Sol 'was used to explore proof strategies for this note ... to review previous approaches to the weaker spectral constant 1+√2 and to identify a possible source of improvement,' while the authors 'developed, verified, and wrote the complete proof themselves,' taking full responsibility — this is exploring-strategy assistance, which under §6.2 is not `generated` or `assisted` mathematics-production, so on its own this second proof's AI role would code as `none`. Because the two results are close in time and address the identical (not merely related) conjecture, I record the event as Jin's July 27 preprint (the one with substantive, authors'-own-account AI production of mathematics), note the Lorist–Schwenninger proof as a corroborating independent line in `disputes`, and set the overall `ai_role` to `assisted` reflecting the more AI-central of the two credited results. As of the latest secondary source found (an August 2026 SIAM News essay by Townsend, and remio.ai's summary), 'neither public manuscript had completed conventional peer review by August 15, 2026' — no journal acceptance, formal referee report, or full expert write-up (e.g., a Tao-blog-style digestion) was found. I searched for later developments (through September 2026) and found none beyond the ByteDance researcher's independent Lean formalization/reproduction efforts on Zenodo (records 22052523 and 22105428, published August 22 and 24, 2026), which likewise remain non-peer-reviewed. Absent a later peer-reviewed acceptance, `claimed` is the correct status.
competing_reading: One could argue the two proofs, having been informally vetted by leading experts in the field including the conjecture's own author (Crouzeix), and independently corroborated by a second, unrelated derivation within eight days, amount to de facto resolution and should be coded `resolved` — informal consensus among the small number of world experts on a niche numerical-analysis question may be the practical ceiling of 'expert digestion' this topic will ever receive, and waiting for a journal to catch up could be coding-by-formality rather than by substance. Against that: §6.1 explicitly requires 'acceptance by a journal of record, or a published verification by named experts' — an informal 'we reviewed it and believe it's correct' relayed through a SIAM News essay and press coverage is short of a published verification, and multiple contemporaneous sources (as late as mid-August 2026) explicitly flag that peer review was still pending for both. I also considered coding Lorist–Schwenninger's proof (arXiv:2608.03841) as the sole primary event with `ai_role: none`, since by their own account AI only suggested strategy; the alternate record would then treat Jin's proof only as a disputed corroborating claim. Both readings are defensible; I chose Jin's proof as primary because it is the more decisive test of AI involvement that this dataset is built to measure, and used `disputes` to preserve the alternative in full.
what_would_settle_it: A journal acceptance notice, a detailed public referee report, or a thorough expert digestion (e.g., a Tao-style blog post or a survey/Notices article) for either the Jin or the Lorist–Schwenninger manuscript would move the status to `resolved`. Absent that, continued silence past several more months without retraction would still leave it `claimed`; an identified error or retraction of either preprint would move that line to `progress`/`incident` while leaving the other claim (if it survives) as the operative `claimed` status.
